mainTopic: The in-between status of a slaughtered, still-twitching animal, and רב הונא on meat scraps attached to a hide
overview: The amud opens at the end of a question: why does a slaughtered, still-twitching non-kosher animal need הכשר to become impure as food, when it will eventually carry the severe impurity of a נבלה? חזקיה answers that its owner could chop it into pieces smaller than a כזית, so severe impurity is not certain. רבי ירמיה points out that חזקיה elsewhere treats such an animal as dead. רבי זירא answers that, for חזקיה, it has left the 'living' category but has not yet entered the 'dead' one. The גמרא then rules like רבי יוחנן, based on רב אושעיא's ברייתא. That ברייתא says a twitching animal gives טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלות, and that parts taken from it count as taken from a living animal. The ברייתא also covers a שחיטה shared between a גוי and a Jew, and a method for eating meat cut before the animal dies. רבי זירא and רב ששת then debate whether the twitching animal protects what it swallowed, and אביי rules strictly both ways. Finally, רב הונא begins explaining the משנה's rule about meat scraps on a hide, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the question: it will eventually carry severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question. A slaughtered, twitching non-kosher animal should be like נבלת עוף טהור, which needs no הכשר because it will eventually carry a severe impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...since in the end it will carry a severe form of impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the גמרא mid-sentence, at the end of a question. The question asks why the twitching animal needs הכשר, when something that will eventually carry severe impurity does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food normally becomes able to receive impurity only after it gets wet (הכשר). But נבלת עוף טהור skips this step, because it will later carry the stronger impurity of a נבלה. The question is: the twitching non-kosher animal will also become a נבלה when it dies, so why should it need הכשר?

keyTerms.meaning: A severe (stronger) form of impurity, like the impurity of a נבלה
Since in the end it will...
Contact with liquid that makes food able to become impure

steps.confusionAlert: This line finishes רבי יוסי's explanation about the carcass of a kosher bird: it needs no הכשר because it can impart severe impurity when eaten. That example strengthens the question about the slaughtered, twitching animal.

phrases.english: since in the end it will impart a severe impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁסּוֹפָהּ לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a twitching, slaughtered non-kosher animal needs הכשר to become impure as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anything that will eventually carry severe impurity (like נבלת עוף טהור) needs no הכשר. This animal will become a נבלה, so it should not need הכשר either.

steps.title: חזקיה: it might never reach severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that the owner could chop the animal into pieces each smaller than a כזית. So it is not certain that it will ever carry the severe impurity of a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: Since he is able to chop it up and bring it down to pieces of less than a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question. The twitching animal is not certain to end up with severe impurity, so it still needs הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה only makes things impure if a piece is at least a כזית. If the owner cuts the animal into tiny pieces while it is still twitching, no piece will ever carry נבלה impurity. Since severe impurity is not guaranteed, the rule about 'it will end up with severe impurity' does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because
To chop it into small pieces
An olive's volume, the minimum size for many impurity and eating laws

steps.whyThisMatters: The key idea is that 'it will eventually be severely impure' only works when that outcome is certain. A mere possibility is not enough.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
since he is able to chop it up,
phrases.notes: He means chopping up the animal while it is still twitching, before it fully dies.

phrases.english: and bring it down to less than an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לְגוֹרְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the severe impurity here is not certain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The twitching animal will surely become a נבלה, just like נבלת עוף טהור, so it should need no הכשר
steps.terutzMaskana: It can be cut into pieces smaller than a כזית, so severe impurity is not guaranteed and הכשר is still needed

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: did חזקיה really say this?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether חזקיה really gave that answer. He points to a dispute about a slaughtered, still-twitching animal, where חזקיה said its limbs are not forbidden as אבר מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Did חזקיה really say this? But it was stated: if someone slaughtered it by cutting both סימנים or most of both, and it is still twitching, חזקיה says: it has no status of limbs (from a living animal). רבי יוחנן says: it does have the status of limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges חזקיה's answer. He quotes another ruling of חזקיה that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this other dispute, the question is whether a twitching animal that was properly slaughtered is still alive, so that a limb taken from it is אבר מן החי. חזקיה says there is no אבר מן החי problem. This sets up the contradiction, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? A way of challenging a statement by pointing to a contradiction
Both סימנים (windpipe and food pipe), or most of both: a proper שחיטה
Twitching; still moving after being slaughtered
Limbs; here, the prohibition of אבר מן החי (a limb from a living animal)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
And did Ḥizkiyya really say this?
But wasn't it stated:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: if he slaughtered in it the two simanim or most of the two,
and it is still twitching –
Ḥizkiyya says: it has no status of limbs,
phrases.notes: Literally 'it is not for limbs': taking a limb from it is not considered taking a limb from a living animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it has the status of limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה הָכִי? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks חזקיה's answer from step 2 using another statement of his
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's answer that the twitching animal is not certain to become severely impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In another place חזקיה treats a slaughtered, twitching animal as no longer living. This clashes with treating it here as something that might never become a נבלה.

steps.title: Spelling out the dispute: dead or not dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two opinions. חזקיה says there is no אבר מן החי problem because the animal counts as dead. רבי יוחנן says there is a problem because it is not yet dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה says it has no status of limbs: it is dead. רבי יוחנן says it has the status of limbs: it is not dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the dispute. This makes the contradiction with חזקיה's earlier answer sharp and clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חזקיה, a properly slaughtered animal counts as dead even while it twitches. If it is already dead, it is already a נבלה with severe impurity. Then chopping it into tiny pieces would not help, and his answer in step 2 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It is considered dead
It is not considered dead
A limb taken from a living animal, forbidden even to a non-Jew

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה holds that a slaughtered, twitching animal already counts as dead. So how could he say it is only possibly going to become a severely impure נבלה? That is רבי ירמיה's challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. חזקיה says 'no limbs' because it is dead. רבי יוחנן says 'limbs' because it is still alive.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya says it has no status of limbs:
it is dead.
Rabbi Yoḥanan says it has the status of limbs:
it is not dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר אֵינָהּ לְאֵבָרִים מֵתָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dispute quoted in step 3, completing the challenge to חזקיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the twitching animal is already dead, it is already a נבלה with severe impurity. So it should need no הכשר, and chopping it up later changes nothing.

steps.title: Neither alive nor dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that, for חזקיה, a twitching slaughtered animal has left the 'living' category but has not yet entered the 'dead' category.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It has left the category of a living animal, but it has not entered the category of a dead animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה's question and shows that חזקיה's two statements do not contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה thought that if חזקיה calls the animal 'dead' for אבר מן החי, it must already count as a נבלה. רבי זירא says there is a middle stage. Because it is no longer 'alive,' there is no אבר מן החי. Because it is not yet 'dead,' it does not yet carry נבלה impurity, so חזקיה can still say it is not certain to become a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: It has left the category of a living animal
The category of a dead animal (a נבלה)

steps.whatToRemember: For חזקיה, a slaughtered, twitching animal is in an in-between state: not alive and not yet dead.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'not alive' must mean 'dead.' The whole answer depends on a third, in-between stage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This middle status explains both rulings of חזקיה at once: no אבר מן החי, and no certain נבלה impurity.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is answering רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: It has left the category of a living animal,
but it has not entered the category of a dead animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָצְתָה מִכְּלַל חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 3-4 against חזקיה's answer in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a third, in-between category that removes the contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the animal is not 'alive' for אבר מן החי, it must already be 'dead' and count as a נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is in between: not alive, so no אבר מן החי, and not yet dead, so no נבלה impurity yet.

steps.title: Back to the dispute about the twitching animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates the dispute: after cutting the סימנים while the animal still twitches, חזקיה says there is no limb prohibition and רבי יוחנן says there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: If one cut the two סימנים, or most of the two, and the animal is still twitching, חזקיה says the limb prohibition does not apply, and רבי יוחנן says it does apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to study the dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן on its own terms. This sets up רבי אלעזר's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the dispute was quoted only as a side point inside a question. Now the גמרא returns to it directly. The question is whether a limb taken from a slaughtered, twitching animal is forbidden as אבר מן החי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself': the גמרא now examines a statement quoted earlier
Both סימנים (windpipe and food pipe), or most of each
Twitching, still moving after slaughter
The prohibition of limbs (אבר מן החי) applies to it

phrases.english: The matter itself:
If one slaughtered it by cutting the two simanim,
or the majority of the two,
and it is still twitching —
Ḥizkiyya says: The prohibition of limbs does not apply to it;
phrases.notes: 'Limbs' here means the איסור of אבר מן החי, eating a limb from a living animal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The prohibition of limbs does apply to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the dispute that was quoted in step 3 and studies it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: חזקיה says no אבר מן החי for a twitching slaughtered animal; רבי יוחנן says there is.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rules like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says to hold onto רבי יוחנן's view, because רב אושעיא teaches a ברייתא that matches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Hold onto רבי יוחנן's view, because רב אושעיא teaches a ברייתא that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר decides the dispute in favor of רבי יוחנן. He says there is a source to back this up, and the next step quotes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a ruling with a reason attached. The reason is a ברייתא from רב אושעיא. So this step depends on how that ברייתא is read in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hold it in your hand': accept this view and rule like it
In line with his view

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Take that opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan in your hand,
as Rav Oshaya teaches a baraita in accordance with his opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקוֹט לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute stated in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יוחנן: a twitching slaughtered animal is still subject to אבר מן החי.

steps.title: רב אושעיא's ברייתא: food impurity, not נבלה impurity
steps.stepSummary: A Jew cuts the סימנים of a non-kosher animal for a non-Jew while it still twitches. It gives food impurity, but not the impurity of נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אושעיא teaches: A Jew who slaughtered a non-kosher animal for a non-Jew, cutting the two סימנים or most of them, while it is still twitching: it gives טומאת אוכלין, but not טומאת נבלות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the beginning of רב אושעיא's ברייתא, which sets up the case. The key proof for רבי יוחנן comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While it twitches, the animal is food, so it can become impure like any food. It is not yet a נבלה, so it does not carry the stronger נבלה impurity. This first part fits both חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher kind of animal
The weaker impurity of ordinary food
The stronger impurity of an animal carcass

phrases.english: As Rav Oshaya teaches:
A Jew who slaughtered a non-kosher animal for a gentile,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: if he cut the two simanim or the majority of the two,
and it is twitching —
it can have the impurity of food,
but not the impurity of carcasses.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that רבי אלעזר relied on in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a twitching slaughtered animal still counts as alive for אבר מן החי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב אושעיא (תוספתא אהלות 2:1).

steps.title: Limbs and flesh count as taken from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says limbs and flesh taken from the twitching animal are treated like parts of a living animal, and are forbidden to בני נח even after it dies. This supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb that comes off it is like one that comes off a living animal. Flesh that comes off it is like flesh that comes off a living animal. It is forbidden to בני נח, even after the animal's life has left it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the ברייתא that proves רבי יוחנן right. It treats the twitching animal as still alive when it comes to parts cut off from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a limb from the twitching animal is 'like from a living animal,' then אבר מן החי applies, which is רבי יוחנן's view. Its being forbidden to בני נח fits this too, since non-Jews are commanded against אבר מן החי. The prohibition stays even after the animal fully dies, because the part was removed while it still counted as alive.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb taken from a living animal
Flesh that comes off a living animal
Non-Jews, who are bound by the seven Noahide laws, including אבר מן החי
When its life leaves it, when it fully dies

steps.whatToRemember: רב אושעיא's ברייתא treats parts taken from a twitching slaughtered animal as taken from a living animal, so we rule like רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Even after its soul departs' does not mean the dead animal itself is forbidden. It means the part removed while it was twitching stays forbidden, even after the animal dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is why רבי אלעזר tells us to rule like רבי יוחנן and not like חזקיה.

phrases.aramaic: אֵבֶר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי,
phrases.english: A limb that separates from it is like one that separates from a living animal,
and flesh that separates from it
is like flesh that separates from a living animal,
and it is forbidden to the descendants of Noah,
even after its soul departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵבֶר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 8 and supplies the actual proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that אבר מן החי applies to a twitching slaughtered animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of רב אושעיא's ברייתא: parts that come off it are like parts from a living animal and are forbidden to בני נח.

steps.title: Partial cut or stabbing of the non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the Jew cut only one סימן or most of one, the twitching animal gives no food impurity. If he stabbed it, it gives no impurity at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut only one sign, or most of one sign, the animal does not give food impurity. If he stabbed it, it has no impurity at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same ברייתא from Step 8. It adds what happens when the slaughter was not done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food impurity in Step 8 came from the fact that both סימנים were cut. With only one סימן, or most of one, the cut does not count, so the animal is not yet food and gives no food impurity. Stabbing (נחירה) is not a slaughter at all, so the living animal has no impurity of any kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of one סימן (windpipe or food pipe)
The impurity that applies to food
Stabbing an animal instead of slaughtering it properly
Any impurity at all

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד, אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד –
phrases.english: If he slaughtered in it one [sign], or most of one –
phrases.notes: Still the Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal for a non-Jew, from Step 8. 'One' means one of the two סימנים.

phrases.english: it does not impart food impurity;
if he stabbed it –
it has no impurity of anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד, אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, now covering a slaughter that was not done properly.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a twitching animal still counts as alive in some ways
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב אושעיא, continued

steps.title: A non-Jew slaughters a kosher animal for a Jew
steps.stepSummary: A parallel case: a non-Jew slaughters a kosher animal for a Jew and it still twitches. It gives food impurity, but not נבלה impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a non-Jew who slaughtered a kosher animal for a Jew, and it is still twitching: it gives food impurity, but not the impurity of a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings a second case that mirrors the first. This time the person slaughtering is a non-Jew and the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered by a non-Jew will become a נבלה. But while it is still twitching it does not yet give נבלה impurity, because it is not fully dead. Still, it counts as food, so it gives food impurity, just like in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
A kosher animal
Twitching after the cut
The impurity of an animal that died without a valid slaughter

phrases.english: And a non-Jew who slaughtered a kosher animal for a Jew,
and it is twitching –
it imparts food impurity,
but not the impurity of a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגוֹי שֶׁשָּׁחַט בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case built just like the first case in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view about a twitching animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב אושעיא, second case

steps.title: Limbs and flesh from it count as from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: A limb or flesh taken from this twitching animal counts as taken from a living animal. It is forbidden to בני נח even after the animal dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb that comes off it is like one coming off a living animal. Flesh that comes off it is like flesh coming off a living animal. And it is forbidden to the descendants of נח, even after the animal dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the same rule for the second case that Step 9 gave for the first. Parts taken from the twitching animal are treated as parts of a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'like from a living animal' means the twitching animal still counts as alive for the limb prohibition. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's view against חזקיה. Because the limb was forbidden when it came off, the animal dying afterward does not make it allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb that comes off the animal
As if it came off a living animal
Non-Jews, who are bound by the seven מצוות of נח, including the ban on a limb from a living animal
Once its life leaves it, after it dies

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the heart of the proof for רבי יוחנן. It shows up in both cases, so the ruling is not a one-time detail.

phrases.english: A limb that separates from it,
is like one separating from a living [animal],
and flesh that separates from it,
is like flesh separating from a living [animal],
and it is forbidden to the descendants of Noah,
and even after its soul departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵבֶר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the limb and flesh rules for the second case, matching Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן: cutting the סימנים while the animal twitches does not remove the limb prohibition

steps.title: Partial cut or stabbing by the non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: If the non-Jew cut only one סימן or most of one, there is no food impurity. If he stabbed it, there is no impurity at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut only one sign, or most of one sign, the animal does not give food impurity. If he stabbed it, it has no impurity at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the second case the same way it ended the first. The Hebrew text really does repeat the line from Step 10, now about the non-Jew's slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without cutting both סימנים, the animal is still simply a living animal, so it is not food and gives no food impurity. Stabbing is not slaughter at all, so there is no impurity of any kind while it lives. The two cases end up exactly alike.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה, the windpipe or the food pipe
Makes things impure

steps.whatToRemember: In both cases (a Jew with a non-kosher animal, or a non-Jew with a kosher animal), a full cut on a twitching animal gives food impurity but not נבלה impurity. Parts taken from it count as from a living animal, which supports רבי יוחנן. A partial cut gives no food impurity, and stabbing gives no impurity at all.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד –
phrases.english: If he slaughtered in it one [sign] or most of one –
phrases.notes: Now the non-Jew slaughtering the kosher animal, from Step 11.

phrases.english: it does not impart food impurity,
if he stabbed it –
it has no impurity of anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second case with the same partial-cut and stabbing rules given in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view about a twitching animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב אושעיא, end of second case

steps.title: A gentile starts the slaughter and a Jew finishes it
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי cuts only a little, not enough to make the animal a טרפה, and a Jew then finishes the שחיטה, the animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a gentile slaughtered in a place that does not make the animal a טרפה, and a Jew came and finished it, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with a new case. A גוי begins cutting, and a Jew completes the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי's cut was small and did no real damage, so it did not make the animal a טרפה. That means the real שחיטה is the Jew's cut, and the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a deadly injury, which makes it forbidden to eat
And he finished it (finished the slaughter)
Kosher, fit to eat

phrases.english: If a gentile slaughtered in a place
that does not make it a tereifa,
and a Jew came and finished it – it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט גּוֹי בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case about a slaughter shared between a גוי and a Jew.
steps.raayaObject: The halacha of a שחיטה started by a גוי and finished by a Jew

steps.title: A Jew starts the slaughter and a gentile finishes it
steps.stepSummary: If a Jew starts the שחיטה and a גוי finishes it, the שחיטה is פסולה, no matter how much the Jew had already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew slaughtered, whether in a place that makes it a טרפה or in a place that does not make it a טרפה, and a gentile came and finished his slaughter, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reverse case: the Jew begins, and the גוי completes the שחיטה. Here the result is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It does not help that the Jew started, even if he already cut a lot. Because the finishing cut was done by a גוי, the שחיטה is not valid. The two cases together show that the person who finishes the שחיטה must be a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid; the שחיטה does not make the animal kosher
Whether... or... (either way)

phrases.english: If a Jew slaughtered,
whether in a place that makes it a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: or in a place that does not make it a tereifa,
and a gentile came and finished his slaughter – it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל, בֵּין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of Step 14. The order is switched, so the result is switched too.
steps.raayaObject: The halacha of a שחיטה started by a Jew and finished by a גוי
steps.whatToRemember: גוי starts and Jew finishes: כשרה (if the גוי's cut did not make it a טרפה). Jew starts and גוי finishes: always פסולה.

steps.title: How to eat meat before the animal fully dies
steps.stepSummary: To eat from an animal before its נפש leaves, cut a כזית of meat from the neck, salt it very well, rinse it very well, and wait until the animal dies. Then both a גוי and a Jew may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who wants to eat from an animal before its soul leaves should cut an olive-size piece of meat from the place of its slaughter, salt it very well, rinse it very well, and wait until its soul leaves, and then eat it. Both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a practical method. It explains how someone can cut meat right after the שחיטה, while the animal is still twitching, and still eat it in a permitted way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat is cut while the animal is still moving, but he does not eat it yet. He salts and rinses it extra well, and he waits until the animal is fully dead before eating. The ברייתא then says that both a גוי and a Jew may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Before its soul leaves, while the animal is still twitching
An olive-size amount
The place of the slaughter cut, the neck
He salts it (to draw out the blood)
He rinses it (to wash off the salt and blood)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he may eat the meat right away. He may cut it early, but he must wait until the animal is fully dead before eating it.

phrases.english: One who wants to eat from an animal
before its soul leaves,
should cut an olive-size piece of meat from the place of its slaughter,
and salt it very well,
and rinse it very well,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַמְתִּין לַהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, וְאוֹכְלוֹ.
phrases.english: and wait for it until its soul leaves, and then eat it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיֹּאכַל מִבְּהֵמָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last clause of the same ברייתא. It moves from who finishes the שחיטה to how to eat from the twitching animal.
steps.raayaObject: The method for eating meat cut before the animal dies
steps.whyThisMatters: This clause is the source the גמרא uses in the next step to support רב אידי בר אבין.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב אידי בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this ברייתא supports רב אידי בר אבין. He taught, in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיין, the same method as advice for staying healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב אידי בר אבין. For רב אידי בר אבין said that רב יצחק בר אשיין said: One who wants to be healthy should cut an olive-size piece of meat from the place of slaughter, salt it very well, rinse it very well, and wait until its soul leaves. Both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps outside the ברייתא and points out that it backs up a teaching of an אמורא, רב אידי בר אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי בר אבין gave this method as health advice: eating this fresh meat is good for you. The ברייתא teaches the very same steps, including the rule that both a גוי and a Jew may eat it. So his teaching now has support from a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him (a source that backs up an אמורא's view)
That he become healthy

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's method (cut from the neck, salt and rinse very well, wait until the animal dies) matches רב אידי בר אבין's health advice, and both say a גוי and a Jew may eat it.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: This supports Rav Idi bar Avin,
for Rav Idi bar Avin said
that Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan said:
One who wants to be healthy,
should cut an olive-size piece of meat from the place of slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמְדִיחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה,
phrases.english: and salt it very well, and rinse it very well,
and wait for it until its soul leaves;

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִים בּוֹ.
phrases.english: both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the last clause of the ברייתא (Step 16) as support for an אמורא's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב אידי בר אבין's teaching in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's clause about eating before the נפש leaves (Step 16)

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks about pausing or pressing during this שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks: if the slaughterer paused (שהיה) or pressed down (דרסה) during this kind of שחיטה, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: If he paused during it, or pressed down during it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a question about the case from the ברייתא, where the animal gets טומאת אוכלין while it is twitching. He wants to know if שהיה or דרסה would ruin this kind of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal שחיטה, pausing or pressing makes the animal a נבלה. Here the שחיטה only makes the animal count as food for טומאה, not kosher for eating. So the question is whether this weaker kind of שחיטה still has to follow every rule of a real שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question; usually a real open question (a dilemma).
He paused in the middle of the שחיטה; this normally makes it invalid.
He pressed the knife down instead of moving it back and forth; this normally makes it invalid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
If he paused during it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the שחיטה from the ברייתא: a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal, or a גוי slaughtering a kosher one.

phrases.english: or pressed down during it, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the ברייתא case of an animal that gets טומאת אוכלין while twitching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the normal things that ruin a שחיטה (שהיה, דרסה) also ruin a שחיטה that only gives the animal the status of food?

steps.title: An elder quotes רבי יוחנן: it needs a proper שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: An elder answers in the name of רבי יוחנן that this case needs a הכשר שחיטה just like a kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: It needs a proper שחיטה, just like a kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: An old sage answers רבי אלעזר's question by quoting רבי יוחנן. This שחיטה must be done properly, the same as when a Jew slaughters a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because it must be like a kosher animal's שחיטה, שהיה or דרסה would ruin it. Then the animal would not get טומאת אוכלין while twitching.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder; an older sage who is not named.
A proper, valid שחיטה done by all the rules.
A kosher animal.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
It needs a proper slaughter
just like a kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שחיטה must be fully valid like a kosher animal's, so שהיה and דרסה would ruin it.

steps.title: What does 'proper שחיטה' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what requirement the words 'proper שחיטה like a kosher animal' are pointing to.
steps.simpleTranslation: A proper שחיטה: for what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רבי יוחנן's words. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'like a kosher animal' sounds like there is some special rule here. The גמרא wants to know exactly which rule this includes.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? What is it referring to?

phrases.english: A proper slaughter: for what?
phrases.notes: What extra rule is רבי יוחנן adding by saying "like a kosher animal"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶכְשֵׁר לְמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word הכשר in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which requirement of a kosher שחיטה does רבי יוחנן mean?

steps.title: It means checking the knife
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק explains that it means בדיקת סכין, checking the knife before the שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: Checking the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers that the extra rule is checking the knife. Even this kind of שחיטה needs a checked knife, just like a kosher one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking the knife makes sure it has no nicks that would tear instead of cut. So this שחיטה must follow even this careful rule of a kosher שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking the knife to make sure it has no nicks.

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that gets טומאת אוכלין from a שחיטה (non-kosher animal by a Jew, or kosher animal by a גוי) still needs a fully proper שחיטה, including a checked knife.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
Checking the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what הכשר means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The knife must be checked before the שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: does the animal protect what it swallowed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רב ששת whether this twitching animal protects the things it swallowed from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רב ששת: Does it protect the swallowed things inside it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a new question about this same twitching animal. Does it protect things it swallowed, like a live animal would, from טומאה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things inside a live animal are protected from טומאה, for example when they are under one roof with a מת. Things inside a dead animal are not protected. So the question is whether this twitching animal counts as alive or dead for this.

keyTerms.meaning: It protects (saves) something from becoming טמא.
Things that were swallowed and are inside the animal.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked of Rav Sheshet:
What is the law: does it protect
the swallowed things that are inside it?
phrases.notes: Picture the twitching animal under one roof with a dead person. Are the things in its stomach still safe from טומאה?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the same twitching animal from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the twitching animal count as alive, so it protects what it swallowed from טומאה?

steps.title: רב ששת: it counts as food, so how could it protect?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers with a rhetorical question. Since the animal is מטמא טומאת אוכלין like a dead animal, how could it protect what is inside it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It imparts the טומאה of food, and it protects?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers no by asking a rhetorical question. The animal is already treated as dead food, since it gets טומאת אוכלין, so it cannot also protect things like a live animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only dead meat can be food for טומאה. Since the ברייתא says this animal gets טומאת אוכלין, it is treated as dead. A dead animal does not protect what is inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: The טומאה that food can get.
It protects.

phrases.english: He said to him: It imparts the impurity of food,
and it protects?!
phrases.notes: This is said in surprise, meaning: of course it doesn't protect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין וּמַצֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question with a rhetorical argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It does not protect, because it is treated as dead food (טומאת אוכלין).

steps.title: רבי זירא pushes back: it isn't a נבלה, so why not protect?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers back that the animal is not מטמא טומאת נבלות, so it is treated as alive. Then it should protect what is inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It does not impart the טומאה of a נבלה, and it does not protect?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רב ששת's answer with a rhetorical question of his own. The animal is not a נבלה, which shows it counts as alive, so it should protect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side points to a different fact from the ברייתא. רב ששת uses טומאת אוכלין to show the animal is dead. רבי זירא uses the fact that it has no טומאת נבלות to show it is alive. אביי settles the argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The טומאה of an animal that died without a proper שחיטה.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the facts from the ברייתא: the animal has טומאת אוכלין but not טומאת נבלות. They only disagree on which fact decides whether it protects what it swallowed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבי זירא is answering רב ששת.

phrases.english: It does not impart the impurity of a carcass,
and it does not protect?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת נְבֵלוֹת וְלֹא תַּצִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's rhetorical answer with an opposite rhetorical argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the animal is treated as dead and does not protect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal is not מטמא טומאת נבלות, which shows it is treated as alive. A live animal protects what is inside it.

steps.title: אביי rules strictly in both directions
steps.stepSummary: אביי settles the debate. The twitching animal does not protect what it swallowed, because it is מטמא טומאת אוכלין. But someone who commits bestiality with it is liable, because it is not מטמא טומאת נבלות and so still counts as alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The animal does not protect the things swallowed inside it, because it can make things impure like food. And someone who commits bestiality with it is liable, because it does not make things impure like a dead animal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי steps in to settle the argument between רבי זירא and רב ששת. He says we go strict on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת looked at one fact: the animal gives טומאת אוכלין, so it seems dead. רבי זירא looked at the other fact: it does not give טומאת נבלות, so it seems alive. אביי uses each fact where it makes the law stricter. For טומאה the animal is treated as dead, so it does not protect what it swallowed. For bestiality it is treated as alive, so the person is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Protects or shields something from becoming impure
Things that were swallowed and are now inside the animal
The lighter impurity that food can carry
The stronger impurity of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
One who commits bestiality with the animal

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's rule: the twitching animal is treated as dead to make things impure, but as alive for the sin of bestiality. Both rulings are the strict one.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not contradicting himself. He does not decide whether the animal is fully 'alive' or fully 'dead.' He takes the strict side in each area of law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא handles an in-between case. When something is partly like one category and partly like another, we can apply the stricter result in each area.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It does not protect the things swallowed inside it,
since it does make things impure with food-impurity,
but one who commits bestiality with it is liable,
since it does not make things impure with the impurity of a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵינָהּ מַצֶּלֶת עַל הַבְּלוּעִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the back-and-forth between רב ששת (step 23) and רבי זירא (step 24) by accepting each one's reasoning in the area where it is stricter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the twitching animal protect what it swallowed from טומאה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, because it is מטמא טומאת אוכלין. But it still counts as alive for bestiality, since it is not מטמא טומאת נבלות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Treat the twitching animal strictly in both directions: dead for protecting what it swallowed, alive for bestiality.

steps.title: רב הונא: the meat scraps count only if someone gathered them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה about אלל, the scraps of meat left on a hide. רב הונא explains that this ruling applies only when a person gathered the scraps together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says, the meat scraps, and so on. רב הונא said: This is only when he gathered them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and starts discussing רבי יהודה's statement about meat scraps on a hide. רב הונא adds a condition: someone must have collected them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says that if the אלל adds up to an olive-sized amount in one place, it carries the טומאה of a נבלה. רב הונא narrows this. The scraps count only if a person gathered them. Gathering them shows he treats them as food, not as part of the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Small scraps of meat left stuck to the hide after skinning
"And that is when he gathered it": a condition limiting the ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's action can decide whether loose scraps count as real food. Whether they count as food decides whether they can carry טומאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The meat scraps, etc.

steps.title: רב הונא: two half-olive pieces on a hide are cancelled out by the hide
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא gives a second rule. Two pieces of נבלה meat, each half an olive in size, that sit on a hide are cancelled out by the hide. This statement continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: Two half-olive pieces that are on top of the hide: the hide cancels them out,
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts a new rule about small pieces of meat attached to a hide. The sentence is not finished here; the גמרא goes on to complete it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece is only half an olive, so neither one alone is big enough to carry the טומאה of a נבלה. Together they would make a full olive's size. But רב הונא says the hide, which does not carry נבלה impurity, cancels them out. So they do not join together.

keyTerms.meaning: Half-olive-sized pieces. A full olive's size is the minimum amount for נבלה impurity
Hide or skin of the animal
Cancels them out, so they lose their own importance

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-olive pieces of נבלה meat on a hide are cancelled out by the hide, so they do not combine into a full olive's size.
